mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q01.stem: The procedure changed, but you have experience with the old one. What should you check before starting?
options: Start every operation using past experience alone.
Check changed hazards, required training and work authority.
Try it yourself if the instructor is absent.
Guess unfamiliar words in the procedure and continue.
reasons: Old-procedure experience does not guarantee new training or permission.
Check hazards and scope before performing authorized work.
This is not a basis for beginning an unconfirmed operation.
Ask about uncertainties before starting.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q02.stem: Which safety check is appropriate after installing a nonslip measure?
options: Assume zero risk simply because it is installed.
Exclude near misses from reporting.
Delete records to reduce the count.
Check reduced slipping and new hazards such as an added step.
reasons: Implementation alone does not establish effectiveness or residual risk.
Minor events also inform improvement.
Deleting records does not prove effectiveness.
Check both the original hazard and side effects.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q03.stem: A chemical container has a corrosion pictogram. What is appropriate for determining handling conditions?
options: Compare product name, precautions, SDS and workplace procedures.
Use identical gloves for all chemicals with that pictogram.
Open the container to check its smell.
Assume one pictogram means no other hazards.
reasons: Connect the pictogram with specific product information and procedures.
Material, concentration and other conditions differ.
Direct investigation of an unknown substance is dangerous.
One symbol cannot exclude other hazards.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q04.stem: An instrument has a JIS mark but unknown calibration status. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: All products automatically pass.
Calibration checks can be omitted permanently.
Check applicability and current management condition.
Use the same method on every material without conditions.
reasons: A standards mark is not a measurement pass for each product.
Damage and calibration need separate checks.
Separate the marking's meaning from current suitability and management.
Suitability for the measurement target must be checked.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q05.stem: Repeatedly using approved, suitable returnable boxes primarily belongs to which 3 R?
options: Only reduction, not reuse.
Recycling, which always destroys the item's form.
Mixing chemical solutions.
Reuse.
reasons: Repeated use of the same item is reuse.
Repeated use as-is differs from reprocessing into resources.
It is unrelated to mixing solutions.
Repeated use under approved conditions is classified as reuse.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q06.stem: What is correct about conclusions from the classification normal salt?
options: Its aqueous solution is always neutral.
The classification alone determines neither pH nor harmlessness.
Any metal salt can be treated like food.
Similarly named salts can be freely substituted.
reasons: A normal salt's solution properties also depend on the combination.
Separate formula-based classification from solution properties and safety.
Check hazards through composition, concentration and other conditions.
Identification and process compatibility need checking.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q07.stem: When combining Fe→Fe²⁺+2 e⁻ and Cu²⁺+2 e⁻→Cu, what is appropriate?
options: Add extra electrons to both sides.
Call both oxidation.
Match electron numbers and check atoms and charges.
Ignore electron position because it is the same as neutralization.
reasons: Match transferred electrons so they cancel.
The electron donor is oxidized; the receiver is reduced.
Check the balance of the overall reaction.
This is redox, distinct from neutralization.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q08.stem: A KYT goal says only be careful. Which improvement is appropriate?
options: Specify who checks what action in which situation.
Remove all equipment measures without returning to hazard identification.
Assume attention makes guards unnecessary.
Never check implementation.
reasons: Connect to executable team actions and checking methods.
This does not justify abandoning necessary engineering measures.
Attention reminders do not replace safety devices.
Check implementation and effectiveness of action goals.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q09.stem: Which use of Heinrich's ratio at work is appropriate?
options: Calculate the next accident probability for every workplace.
Use it to emphasize reporting and addressing minor hazards.
A major accident cannot happen before 300 events.
Alter reports when the ratio does not match.
reasons: It does not guarantee universal accident probabilities.
Connect it to prevention rather than mechanical prediction.
It does not guarantee an accident-free event count.
Actual facts must not be changed.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q10.stem: The current field requires A, but the display was 250 mA. Which conversion is correct?
reasons: m means one thousandth.
The conversion direction is reversed.
It is not a one-place conversion.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q11.stem: What is appropriate when checking a packaging improvement?
options: Use total waste alone even when production quantities differ.
Judge from collection-box color alone.
Compare usage and effects on defects under the same conditions.
Remove all protective packaging without approval to save resources.
reasons: Consider differences in target quantities and periods.
Color is not an effectiveness indicator.
Check quality, safety and adjacent processes as well as resources.
Changing necessary protection requires approval and suitability checks.

mfg1-surface-weekly-07-q12.stem: Which explanation distinguishes H⁺+OH⁻→H₂O from the redox reaction studied here?
options: The elements' oxidation numbers do not change in this neutralization.
Every water-forming reaction is metal deposition.
No color change means no chemical reaction.
Call both electron donors and receivers reduced.
reasons: Distinguish oxidation-number changes and electron transfer.
Do not equate neutralization with metal deposition.
Appearance alone cannot establish whether a reaction occurs.
Losing electrons is oxidation.
